chunks: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who killed a pigeon from the pigeons of the Ḥaram while he was in iḥrām, and he said:

"If he killed it while he was in iḥrām in the Ḥaram, then a sheep is due from him, and the value of the pigeon is one dirham. If he killed it in the Ḥaram while he was not in iḥrām, then its value is due from him, which is one dirham, which he gives in charity or with which he buys food for the pigeons of the Ḥaram. And if he killed it while he was in iḥrām outside the Ḥaram, then the blood-sacrifice of a sheep is due from him."

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the Sacred Sanctuary, whose inviolability affects the ruling
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: the sacrificial blood-offering of a sheep
key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: one dirham, the specified value of the pigeon
key_terms.شَاةٌ: a sheep given as expiatory sacrifice
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of iḥrām for hajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a pigeon of the Ḥaram while in iḥrām or inside the Sacred Sanctuary?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal rulings for killing a pigeon belonging to the Sacred Sanctuary under different conditions. The expiation differs depending on whether the person was in iḥrām, inside the Ḥaram, or both, showing the added sanctity of both iḥrām and the Ḥaram. It also mentions monetary compensation and directing that value toward charity or feeding the pigeons of the Ḥaram.
